pattern: no COM port|No serial data received|could not open port|FileNotFoundError
cause: Windows sees no USB device: a charge-only cable or a loose USB-C plug (LEDs on, board looks alive).
fix: Swap the cable at the laptop end, then at the board end (a data cable, not charge-only).
Reseat the USB-C plug; check Device Manager > Ports (COM & LPT).

pattern: Access is denied|PermissionError|port is busy|in use
cause: Another program holds the COM port (serial monitor, a stuck earlier run).
fix: Close the serial monitor and any running python run.py.
Unplug and replug the board if the handle is stuck.

cause: A stale node: a run that ended abruptly leaves the SafetyNode active and silent until reset. Otherwise the wrong port or wrong firmware.
fix: The preflight pulses EN through RTS once; if still silent, press RESET on the board.
Check the COM port against health/inventory.json (B = COM13, A = COM14).
Reflash with scripts/hil_flash.py if the sketch is wrong.

pattern: CAN FAILED|FAILED - PiL only|MCP2515 not answering
cause: The MCP2515 does not answer on SPI: worn Dupont jumpers caused every hardware fault in bring-up (once cleared by a reflash, cause unknown).
fix: Replace the SPI jumpers with FRESH wires (reseating is not enough on a worn one).
Run hil/firmware/SpiProbe to separate a dead module from a floating line.
Reflash the board and read the hello again.

pattern: is not the inventory|older than the source
cause: The board runs firmware other than the inventory expects, e.g. the ESP32 was not reflashed after v2.6.
fix: python scripts/hil_flash.py --b COM13 --a COM14
If the flash was deliberate, update health/inventory.json.

cause: Board A (the observer) stopped reporting while B was powered: the CAN link dropped, or A hung. Without this call it shows up as dozens of false FAILs.
fix: Check the CAN pair (CANH/CANL), the 120 ohm termination and the MCP2515 jumpers on both boards.
Rerun: the bench treats it as a bench fault and recovers the boards.

cause: The CH340 bridge has no flow control: a burst of frames overflows the receive buffer (A's own busy-waits, v2.9.8) or the PC reads too slowly.
fix: Keep BusNode >= 2.6 (CAN reception in its own task and a 256-frame queue).
Do not run a heavy job on the laptop during the campaign; plug in the charger.

pattern: Failed to connect|Wrong boot mode|waiting for download
cause: The ESP32 did not enter download mode for the upload.
fix: Hold BOOT, tap RESET (EN), release BOOT, run the command again.

pattern: text section exceeds|region .* overflowed|Sketch too big
cause: The firmware no longer fits the app partition.
fix: Build with -Os (default) and drop unused code.
Pick a larger app partition scheme before adding features.

cause: A board did not answer a TesterPresent / ReadDataByIdentifier request on the CAN bus: firmware without UDS (older than SafetyNode 2.7 / BusNode 2.8), a dead CAN link, or no second node to ACK the request.
fix: Read the USB hello first: it names the firmware.
Reflash with scripts/hil_flash.py if the version has no UDS.
Check the CAN pair and termination.
